theorem_title: Complete wanted-pair setup from signed source arrays
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightWantedSetup.program_meets {μ : ℕ → ℤ} {a b NL NR M free U D d : ℕ} {shift : ℤ}
    (left right : ℕ → ℤ) (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hM : 0 < M)
    (ha : a+NL ≤ free) (hb : b+NR ≤ free)
    (hspace : _root_.ThreeSum.LightWantedSetup.space free M left right NL NR U D shift ≤ lim.space)
    (hword : (_root_.ThreeSum.LightSourceResidues.word M M U D : ℤ) ≤ lim.word)
    (hshift : |shift| ≤ (D : ℤ)) (hd : d+NL+5 ≤ lim.depth)
    (hleft : ∀ i < NL, μ (a+i)=left i) (hright : ∀ j < NR, μ (b+j)=right j)
    (hvaluesL : ∀ i < NL, |left i| ≤ (U : ℤ))
    (hvaluesR : ∀ j < NR, |right j| ≤ (U : ℤ)) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightWantedSetup.program 11 d [a,b,NL,NR,M,shift,free] μ (_root_.ThreeSum.LightWantedSetup.time M left right NL NR U D shift)
      (fun r ν => r=(free : ℤ) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightWantedSetup.Output ν free M left right NL NR shift ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ν free) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let two stored signed arrays have lengths $N_L,N_R$ and absolute values bounded by $U$, let modulus $M>0$, and let shift $s$ satisfy $|s|\le D$. Assume both inputs end before the free address, the exact setup allocation and source-residue word bound hold, addresses fit words, and depth $d+N_L+5$ is available. The closed program computes residues and buckets and writes the complete wanted output contract, including all original-position pairs satisfying $M\mid a_i+s-b_j$, in its stated time. It returns the header address and preserves the input prefix.

Constructs the exact shifted join without supplied residue or bucket advice. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
